segments.text: Bangalore. Two friends. Same age, same salary.
segments.caption: Bangalore. Two friends. Same age, same salary.

segments.text: And from their parents, the same gift: twenty-five lakh rupees each.
segments.caption: And from their parents, the same gift: ₹25 lakh each.

segments.text: One will buy. One will rent. Only one will win.
segments.caption: One will buy. One will rent. Only one will win.

segments.text: Arjun, beta, rent is money thrown away! Buy a flat. Property never goes down!
segments.caption: Arjun beta, rent is money thrown away! Buy a flat. Property never goes down!

segments.text: Okay Papa. A ninety lakh flat. Twenty-five lakh down, the rest on a home loan.
segments.caption: Okay Papa. A ₹90 lakh flat. ₹25 lakh down, the rest on a home loan.

segments.text: His EMI: sixty-two thousand five hundred. Every month. For twenty years.
segments.caption: His EMI: ₹62,500. Every month. For twenty years.

segments.text: Twenty years?!
segments.caption: Twenty years?!

segments.text: Meera, everyone is buying. Why are you renting like a student?
segments.caption: Meera, everyone is buying. Why are you renting like a student?

segments.text: Maa, rent is only twenty-one thousand. My twenty-five lakh goes into an index fund.
segments.caption: Maa, rent is only ₹21,000. My ₹25 lakh goes into an index fund.

segments.text: And every month, I invest the forty-five thousand I save.
segments.caption: And every month, I invest the ₹45,000 I save.

segments.text: Hey Bhagwan.
segments.caption: Hey Bhagwan.

segments.text: Five years pass.
segments.caption: Five years pass.

segments.text: Meera's money grows to seventy-eight lakh. Arjun's share of his flat: fifty-one.
segments.caption: Meera's money grows to ₹78 lakh. Arjun's share of his flat: ₹51 lakh.

segments.text: See, Maa?
segments.caption: See, Maa?

segments.text: And then, in year six, the market crashes. Thirty-five percent.
segments.caption: And then, in year six, the market crashes. 35%.

segments.text: I told you!
segments.caption: I told you!

segments.text: Meera, you lost twenty-three lakh! Now I'm ahead.
segments.caption: Meera, you lost ₹23 lakh! Now I'm ahead.

segments.text: Only on paper, Arjun. I'm not selling. I keep investing, every single month.
segments.caption: Only on paper, Arjun. I'm not selling. I keep investing, every single month.

segments.text: Twenty years later.
segments.caption: Twenty years later.

segments.text: My flat is fully paid. Worth two point four crore!
segments.caption: My flat is fully paid. Worth ₹2.4 crore!

segments.text: And my portfolio, four point one crore.
segments.caption: And my portfolio: ₹4.1 crore.

segments.text: But here is the twist.
segments.caption: But here is the twist.

segments.text: If Meera had panicked and sold in that crash, she would have ended with only two point six crore.
segments.caption: If Meera had panicked and sold in that crash, she'd have ended with only ₹2.6 crore.

segments.text: One panic. One and a half crore, gone.
segments.caption: One panic. ₹1.5 crore, gone.

segments.text: And if flat prices had grown eight percent a year instead of five, Arjun would have won.
segments.caption: And if flat prices had grown 8% a year instead of 5%, Arjun would have won.

segments.text: So the moral of the story: renting does not beat buying. Discipline does.
segments.caption: Moral of the story: renting doesn't beat buying. Discipline does.

segments.text: And no landlord can ever ask me to leave!
segments.caption: And no landlord can ever ask me to leave!

segments.text: Fair point, Arjun.
segments.caption: Fair point, Arjun.
